speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you're experiencing weakness and fatigue; to help me narrow this down, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any accompanying issues like fever, weight loss, or changes in your bowel habits?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count (CBC)  
REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel (CMP)

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unusual, as a urinary tract infection typically presents with burning during urination and frequency rather than diplopia; can you describe your double vision—does it affect one or both eyes, and does it worsen when you look up? While we discuss that, please have your CBC and CMP results prepared for review.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history provided. Social history: Enjoys outdoor activities such as hiking and camping. No mention of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Please confirm if your double vision improves when you close one eye, and have you noticed any recent muscle twitching or drooping eyelids? Additionally, I need to see the preliminary results from the CBC and CMP we ordered to rule out systemic causes.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, headache, or any respiratory, gastrointestinal, or urinary symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of diplopia worsening with upward gaze combined with fatigue and the absence of other systemic symptoms makes a neuromuscular junction disorder like Myasthenia Gravis the most likely diagnosis. Please have the CBC and CMP results ready, and we will proceed with specific antibody testing and imaging if needed.
